chain.g: to take possession of; invest (person, court)

ety.text: Earlier seise, from Middle English seisen, sesen, saisen, from Old French seisir (“to take possession of; invest (person, court)”), from Early Medieval Latin sacīre (“to lay claim to, appropriate”) (8th century) in the phrase ad propriam sacire, from Old Low Frankish *sakjan (“to sue, bring legal action”), from Proto-Germanic *sakjaną, *sakōną (compare Old English sacian (“to strive, brawl”)), from Proto-Germanic *sakaną (compare Old Saxon sakan (“to accuse”), Old High German sahhan (“to bicker, quarrel, rebuke”), Old English sacan (“to quarrel, claim by law, accuse”).

senses.d: To deliberately take hold of; to grab or capture.
To take advantage of (an opportunity or circumstance).
To take possession of (by force, law etc.).
ex: to seize smuggled goods
to seize a ship after libeling

senses.d: To have a sudden and powerful effect upon.
ex: a panic seized the crowd
a fever seized him

senses.d: To bind, lash or make fast, with several turns of small rope, cord, or small line.
ex: to seize two fish-hooks back to back
to seize or stop one rope on to another

senses.d: To fasten, fix.
To lay hold in seizure, by hands or claws (+ on or upon).
ex: to seize on the neck of a horse
The text which had seized upon his heart with such comfort and strength abode upon him for more than a year.

senses.d: To have a seizure.
To bind or lock in position immovably; see also seize up.
ex: Rust caused the engine to seize, never to run again.

senses.d: To submit for consideration to a deliberative body.

senses.d: The act of taking possession, as by force or right of law.
ex: the seizure of a thief, a property, a throne, etc.

senses.d: The state of being seized or of having been taken.
ex: The continued seizure of the car is a violation of my rights.

senses.d: That which is seized, or taken possession of; a thing laid hold of, or possessed.
ex: The seizure includes various belongings taken from his house and his office.

senses.d: A retention within one's grasp or power; possession; ownership.
ex: Make o'er thy honour by a deed of trust, / And give me seizure of the mighty wealth.

senses.d: A sudden onset of pain or emotion.
ex: He felt the seizure of pain when the heart attack began.

senses.d: A sudden attack or convulsion; the physical manifestation of the abnormal electrical discharges in the brain characteristic of epilepsy.
ex: epileptic seizure
I haven't had a seizure since I started that medication.
